# Transaction Results Checklist: Unified Table Processing and Atomic Transaction Optimization

**Purpose**: Review whether the written requirements for atomic commit, snapshot safety, commit folding, dirty reads, deletes and live history, flush and transfer budgets, and plan-cache identity are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-10-27
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are group-commit requirements specified so one accepted nonempty transaction covers every touched table, main row, index, required history, and durable effect intent in its supported domain? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Spec §US1 scenario 1]
- [x] CHK002 Are late validation failure, rollback, and interrupted commit or replay required to leave no partial durable row, index, history, file, or success notification? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-012, Spec §US1 scenarios 2 and 5]
- [x] CHK003 Are pinned snapshot reads required to keep their committed frontier across later writes, flush, and compaction, including hot-only, cold-only, and mixed tiers? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, Spec §US1 scenario 3, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK004 Are cross-domain commits, incompatible backends, and exceeded byte, row, and version limits required to fail before any partial write, without a silent split? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Spec §US1 scenario 4, Contract §1]
- [x] CHK005 Are all nine fold transitions specified, including explicit null, duplicate-key handling, reinsertion, primary-key rename, savepoint rollback, and savepoint release? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, Spec commit-fold table, Contract §2]
- [x] CHK006 Are dirty-transaction reads required to preserve partial-patch meaning, authorization, joins, aggregates, order, limits, and both directions of predicate movement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016, Spec §US3 scenario 2]
- [x] CHK007 Are deleted rows required to keep the payload queries and change delivery need, with primary-key lookup seeing the latest tombstone and ordinary secondary indexes omitting new tombstones only after a complete authoritative path exists? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, Spec §FR-020, Spec §US4 scenarios 1 and 2]
- [x] CHK008 Are complete-event replay and latest-state-since-cursor reads specified as distinct contracts, including domain order and an explicit gap or resynchronization when history is expired, overloaded, or incompatible? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018, Spec §US4 scenario 3, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK009 Are index rebuild, concurrent writes, failover, and recovery required to publish one generation atomically without dropping snapshot or history retention? [Completeness, Spec §FR-021, Spec §US4 scenario 4]
- [x] CHK010 Are ordinary same-scope writes required to record pending work without waiting on bulk cold storage, while final publication stays synchronized and unique? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022, Spec §US5 scenario 1]
- [x] CHK011 Are flush, compaction, and transfer required to stay inside declared memory and concurrency budgets, to reclaim inactive coordination state, and to keep one synchronization authority per active scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023, Spec §FR-025, Spec §US5 scenarios 2 and 3]
- [x] CHK012 Are plan-cache identity, concurrent-miss coordination, and structured reuse for description, execution, and routing specified for equivalent SQL under different session contexts? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027, Spec §FR-028, Spec §FR-029, Spec §US6]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK013 Is "one atomic storage submission" defined so per-row or per-table commits do not qualify, and so a truly empty or no-op commit may submit zero times while preserving original statement results? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Spec Assumptions]
- [x] CHK014 Is the snapshot frontier defined as the committed visibility boundary and version domain a pinned reader keeps, rather than a global order or a timestamp? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, Spec Key Entities, Spec Assumptions]
- [x] CHK015 Is commit folding defined so the final stored state may collapse while statement results, savepoint history, and separately promised complete events stay intact? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-018, Spec commit-fold table]
- [x] CHK016 Is a reused scanned target required to be checked against the authoritative committed version, and are target handles excluded from acting as authorization? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Spec §US3 scenario 3]
- [x] CHK017 Is "positive median improvement" defined as the median beating the measured baseline run-to-run spread across at least five matched repeats, with each runtime reported in seconds? [Clarity, Spec §SC-009, Spec §FR-036]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK018 Do FR-006, User Story 1 scenario 1, and SC-001 require the same outcome: one submission for each supported nonempty commit, zero partial outcomes, and the original affected counts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Spec §US1 scenario 1, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK019 Do the commit-fold table, FR-014, and User Story 3 scenario 1 agree on preserved statement results, savepoints, explicit null, untouched fields, and duplicate-key errors? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, Spec §US3 scenario 1, Spec commit-fold table]
- [x] CHK020 Do FR-020 and User Story 4 scenario 2 agree that omitted secondary-index tombstones still have a complete path for deleted-row and history queries? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, Spec §US4 scenario 2]
- [x] CHK021 Do FR-022 and User Story 5 scenario 1 agree that bulk cold I/O stays off the lock ordinary writes need for pending-work registration? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, Spec §US5 scenario 1]
- [x] CHK022 Do FR-027 and User Story 6 scenario 1 agree that sessions with different system-column visibility cannot reuse one wildcard projection? [Consistency, Spec §FR-027, Spec §US6 scenario 1]
- [x] CHK023 Do FR-007, the stated delivery order, and the Story 3 checkpoint agree that folding stays disabled until uncoalesced atomic commit is proven? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Spec Assumptions, tasks.md Story 3 checkpoint]
- [x] CHK024 Does SC-009 withhold its 5% allowance from system-catalog paths and point those paths at SC-015, so transaction work cannot trade catalog latency? [Consistency, Spec §SC-009, Spec §SC-015]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK025 Can atomicity and snapshot safety be decided from SC-001 and SC-002, including the 25,000-row cases, one submission, zero partial outcomes, and hot, cold, and mixed tiers? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK026 Can folding and dirty reads be decided from SC-003 and SC-010, including every fold transition, 25,000 operations on one key, and exact results for 100-read and 1,000-read workloads? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, Spec §SC-010]
- [x] CHK027 Can background work and cache behavior be decided from SC-006, SC-007, and SC-008, including three 10-minute runs, a 10x scope-churn tolerance, a 1-second delayed cold operation, both warmup orders, and safe release of cancelled or failed leaders? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006, Spec §SC-007, Spec §SC-008]

- [x] CHK029 Are long-lived snapshots and an unset snapshot frontier addressed for update, delete, flush, compaction, reclamation, and restart? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-009, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK030 Are the same typed key across tables or users, explicit null versus an absent field, and primary-key rename collisions addressed? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-014, Spec Edge Cases, Spec commit-fold table]
- [x] CHK031 Are failed publication, transfer cancellation, and lock reclamation racing holders and waiters addressed? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-012, Spec §FR-024, Spec §FR-025, Spec Edge Cases]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK032 Are cross-domain transactions, new SQL constraint families, Row V2 writer activation, and the stable-primary-key secondary-index redesign excluded from this activation and gated on their own decisions? [Assumption, Spec §FR-031, Spec Assumptions]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [x] CHK034 Is a nonempty commit defined so an insert followed by a delete that leaves no durable state, history, or effect intent is not forced to invent a storage submission? [Ambiguity, Spec Assumptions]
- [x] CHK035 Does SC-004 limit replay success to the absence of duplicate logical durable effects, and decline a universal network exactly-once guarantee? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-004, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK036 Do the tasks that allow explicit stream transactions and that place stream rows and persisted-system mutations in the same storage batch agree with the spec rule that explicit stream transactions stay rejected and that a mixed commit is only user and shared inside one compatible domain? [Conflict, Spec §US2 scenario 3, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-008, Spec Assumptions, tasks.md T013, tasks.md T067]
- [ ] CHK037 Does the plan's localized stream engine, limited to append, expiry, and hard delete, agree with T013, which allows explicit stream transactions and moves stream storage onto the versioned engine? [Conflict, Plan summary, tasks.md T013]
- [ ] CHK038 Does User Story 1, which specifies the atomic commit for user and shared tables, agree with the Phase 4 task goal that also places persisted-system direct-API mutations in that batch, while User Story 2 scenario 4 still rejects explicit SQL transactions on persisted system tables? [Conflict, Spec §US1, Spec §US2 scenario 4, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-043, tasks.md Phase 4, tasks.md T067]

## Notes

- Scope chosen for this review: User Story 1 plus User Stories 3–6. Catalog projections, shared-table row-level security, and the unified storage design stay in `catalog-rls.md` and `unified-table-design.md`.
- Depth: standard review. Audience: spec author, before implementation.
- Checked items were marked on 2026-10-27 because the cited spec, assumption, or contract text answers the question. A check records requirements quality only. It does not record that implementation or performance acceptance is done (Spec §SC-012).
- CHK036 stays open. Spec §US2 scenario 3, §FR-004, §FR-008, and the assumptions keep explicit stream transactions rejected and limit mixed commits to user and shared tables in one compatible domain. tasks.md T013 allows explicit stream transactions, and the Story 1 goal plus T067 put stream rows and persisted-system direct-API mutations into that same batch. Those task lines need to be reconciled with the spec before this item can be checked.
- CHK037 and CHK038 were appended to split that conflict. CHK037 asks whether the plan's append-only stream engine agrees with T013. CHK038 asks whether a persisted-system direct-API mutation may join the user/shared batch that User Story 1 specifies, given that explicit SQL transactions on persisted system tables stay rejected. Both remain unchecked.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
